daily_reports.label: Mon 9 Nov 2026 (London)
daily_reports.source: Buffer read 10 Nov ~07:35 London (X metrics 04:02, Facebook 04:07, YouTube 06:19; 21:30 posts had 6 to 10 hours live, so Facebook and YouTube numbers for them are early). 7-day average = per post, posts published 2 to 8 Nov (X 23 posts, YouTube 13, Facebook 27). Whop read 10 Nov ~07:40 London.
daily_reports.verdict_why: Whop on pace, social reach below average. Month to date (day 10 of 30): 345 Whop visits vs about 333 by today (on pace; 64 visits on 9 Nov was the second best day of the month), 6 Pro trials vs about 1.7 (ahead), 1 new paid vs about 0.7 (ahead), Free Master Class sign-ups 0 vs about 10 (behind). On 9 Nov none of the 9 channel posts beat its 7-day average except the X stat card, which matched it (37 vs 38.4). No new trial or paid member on the day.
daily_reports.best: YouTube 13:30 "When buy Demand ends": 27 views and 1 like (3.7% engagement), the most-watched post of the day, though still under the 53.5 average (median 36). The 21:30 "Tight stops tested worst" video was the only post with comments on two channels (1 on X, 1 on YouTube) even with just 31 and 7 views so far.
daily_reports.worst: YouTube 21:30 "Tight stops tested worst": 7 views after about 10 hours, against 29 for "One wick is not a body close" at the same age the day before. Facebook 09:00 stat card: 0 impressions for the second day running, and the Facebook 21:30 reel shows 1 impression (Facebook figures lag, so it may rise).
daily_reports.followers: X followers 553 (552 on 9 Nov, +1). YouTube subscribers 616 (616 on 9 Nov, flat). No Facebook follower count available through Buffer.
daily_reports.whop: 64 store visits on 9 Nov (41 on 8 Nov, 345 since 1 Nov; 6 so far on 10 Nov). 0 new trials and 0 new paid on 9 Nov; 1 Free Mastery claim at 18:43. No cash collected and no failed payment on 9 Nov. Overnight 10 Nov: the Perfect Entry $70 retry failed again and Whop canceled that membership at 03:32 London (MRR 2,147.54 to 2,077.54). No trial ends within 48 hours.
learned: Whop visits hit 64 on a day with only 7 views on the new YouTube Short and no tagged traffic (127 of 129 site visitors since 1 Nov carry no utm tag), so we still cannot say where visit spikes come from.
Posts that ask for a reply (Spot the Candle #4) got 33 X impressions and 0 replies, so the question alone did not pull answers; the myth-style video titles are the ones that got comments.
Facebook reach is near zero for image posts (0 and 2 impressions) and low for reels (1 to 4 on 9 Nov), against 42 for the 8 Nov reel.
suggestions: Put the tagged Whop links (utm_source youtube, x, facebook) in every caption and in the YouTube and X bios this week so the next visit or trial spike can be traced. Changes to scheduled captions need Max's OK.

Move the Spot the Candle answer and other quiz posts onto the chart image with a one-line question inside the picture, and ask for a single word reply; it got 0 replies yesterday. Keep plain stat cards off the schedule (Max asked to stop them); the 11 Nov 09:00 X stat card is still scheduled and could be swapped for a chart prompt.

Reuse the title style that drew comments ("One wick is not a body close", "Tight stops tested worst") on the 13:30 YouTube slot, which averaged 27 to 21 views this week, and test one 13:30 Short as a hook-first claim to see if views go above the 36 median.
